title: Skip D3: late three-cofactor dichotomy, exact survivor certificates, and the auxiliary late-only ratchet

concepts.label: Late largest false rank
concepts.description: A row has a skipped rank d whose maximal false rank remains in the terminal zone 2s<3d.

concepts.label: Three-cofactor boundary
concepts.description: Among ranks below s dividing 2s+1 or 2s+2, only quotient cofactor three can enter the late zone; the half-row cofactor cannot.

concepts.label: Kernel-computable greedy-row certificate
concepts.description: A structural-recursive copy of the seam weights and a Boolean row check whose truth certifies the largest false rank.

concepts.label: Seven measured survivor classes
concepts.description: The classes D=101,122,164,314,545,629,1112 selected by an external depth-25 scan; their selection is measured context, while the listed Lean certificates are proved.

concepts.label: Angle B2 cofactor-window hypothesis
concepts.description: Selection of every AngleB2 cofactor rank on the three rows D+1,D+2,D+3, an antecedent of the separate conditional connection theorem.

concepts.label: Late-only cofactor floor
concepts.description: The pulse contribution certified using only selected cofactor-three ranks, smaller than the full Angle B2 floor.

concepts.label: Late-only auxiliary ratchet
concepts.description: A recurrence driven by the late-only floor; it is an auxiliary lower-bound model and is not identified unconditionally with the concrete below-pulse orbit.

concepts.label: Ratchet threshold twelve
concepts.description: Because the late total floor is at most eleven, any late-only budget at least twelve persists and can never reach zero.

concepts.label: Period 2730
concepts.description: The common period inherited from the pulse floor and the modulo-three late-cofactor contribution.

concepts.label: Cofinal late-row supply
concepts.description: Late largest skips occurring at arbitrarily large rows, strong enough to yield unbounded skipped ranks.

concepts.label: Mersenne half-membership endpoint
concepts.description: Membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set; this is the #257 endpoint used here, not a proved theorem without a cofinal supply.

concepts.label: Measured/proved boundary
concepts.description: Finite scan observations motivate the seven classes, but only the explicit declarations and their quantified consequences carry Lean proof authority.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A skipped rank m with 2<=m<s and 2s<3m forces the row's largest false rank to be late. At every s>=4 either all late ranks are selected or such a late largest skip exists. For divisors of 2s+1 or 2s+2 below s, the only ranks capable of lying in that zone are the two cofactor-three solutions; the half-row cofactor is never late.
statement_nodes.engine: maximal false-rank extraction from a finite interval plus elementary quotient arithmetic
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Source-authoritative formalisation only; no novelty or historical priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The dichotomy does not prove that late skips occur cofinally. Enlarging the divisor list beyond cofactor three cannot strengthen this particular late-zone argument.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The structurally recursive weight list wgt equals the well-founded seam-weight recursion with sufficient fuel. Consequently the Boolean word gb is the concrete seam greedy word, has length s-2, and its bit lookup exactly decides support membership. The Boolean rowChk certifies that d is the largest false rank and, with 2s<3d, certifies LargestSkipLateAt s.
statement_nodes.engine: structural recursion, equality to the original well-founded recursion, Boolean support lookup, and kernel evaluation
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is executable proof infrastructure internal to the formal development.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: rowChk proves only the explicitly evaluated rows. Its executability is not a uniform theorem that late skips exist.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For each D in {101,122,164,314,545,629,1112}, all three rows s=D+1,D+2,D+3 have a kernel-checked late largest false rank. The certified ranks are 101,101,101; 121,123,124; 162,165,166; 314,315,316; 545,546,546; 628,630,630; and 1111,1113,1114 respectively.
statement_nodes.engine: twenty-one exact rowChk evaluations by decide +kernel
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A finite verified table, not an asymptotic theorem.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The seven values were chosen by an external scan, but the Lean authority here is only the twenty-one displayed row certificates. A finite table supplies no cofinal late-row sequence.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: At rows 103,124,166,316,547,631,1114 the respective odd three-cofactors 69,83,111,211,365,421,743 are absent from the greedy support. Each skip independently forces LargestSkipLateAt at that row, without relying on the maximal-rank rowChk computation.
statement_nodes.engine: seven Boolean support checks followed by the universal skipped-three-cofactor implication
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A second finite proof route for seven rows, recorded because it exposes the structural cofactor mechanism.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: These seven isolated rows do not establish eventual or cofinal failure of three-cofactor selection.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every D in {101,122,164,314,545,629,1112}, the Angle B2 hypothesis requiring all cofactor ranks to be selected throughout rows D+1,D+2,D+3 is false. Explicit skipped witnesses are 69 at row 103, 62 at 123, 83 at 165, 158 at 315, 365 at 547, 421 at 631, and 557 at 1113.
statement_nodes.engine: explicit kernel-checked missing-support witnesses contradicting the three-row universal selection hypothesis
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A finite inapplicability certificate for one conditional route.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Failure of an antecedent blocks the Angle B2 connection theorem on these seven windows; it does not prove the negation of that theorem's conclusion and does not resolve #257.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: On each of the twenty-one rows in the seven three-row windows, cofRanks selection or LargestSkipLateAt holds through the right, late-skip disjunct; and the bundled theorem records that the full three-row hcof hypothesis fails for every one of the seven D values.
statement_nodes.engine: finite case split over seven D values and three row positions, consuming the exact row and hcof certificates
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Bundling of the exact finite results above.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorem is restricted to seven named classes and twenty-one rows. It is not a global dichotomy for AngleB2.cofRanks.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every s>=5, either both ranks solving 3m=2s+1 or 3m=2s+2 are selected by the concrete seam greedy word, or the row has a late largest false rank.
statement_nodes.engine: classical excluded middle on selection of the two cofactor-three solutions, with any failure promoted to a late largest skip
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The source proves this unconditional rowwise dichotomy; no external priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The left branch selects only the late cofactor-three ranks, not all AngleB2.cofRanks. The theorem does not determine which branch occurs cofinally.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: lateCofRanks contains precisely the applicable cofactor-three rank when s is 1 or 2 modulo 3, with certified pulse floor 2 or 1 respectively and zero otherwise. For s>=61 these ranks lie above 26 and are disjoint from the eight fixed small ranks. If every late cofactor rank is selected, lateTotalFloor=pulseFloor+lateCofFloor is bounded by the concrete belowPulse; uniformly lateCofFloor<=2 and lateTotalFloor<=11.
open_antecedents: For the sound lower bound at a row, every rank in lateCofRanks s must actually be selected by the concrete seam greedy word.
statement_nodes.engine: modulo-three classification, divisor pulse lower bounds, disjoint finite sums, and the existing fixed-rank pulse floor
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This is strictly the late-only floor, not AngleB2.totalFloor. On the seven measured classes the required selection hypothesis fails at the exhibited rows, so the auxiliary floor cannot simply be identified with their concrete contribution.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The auxiliary lateRun starts at 3 and evolves by lateStep using lateTotalFloor. Zero is absorbing. Because lateTotalFloor<=11, a value at least 12 remains at least 12 forever; in particular, reaching 12 by depth four guarantees nonzero value at every depth.
statement_nodes.engine: elementary recurrence inequalities around the uniform floor bound eleven
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Exact theorem about the auxiliary recurrence defined in this module.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Persistence of lateRun is not persistence of the concrete belowPulse orbit unless the separate selected-late-cofactor hypothesis connects the floor to the row.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Kernel computation gives lateRun D 4 equal to 24,24,21,24,24 for D=20,314,545,629,1112, so all five phases are nonzero at every depth. In contrast, lateRun D 3=0 for D=101,122,164, hence those three auxiliary runs remain zero thereafter.
statement_nodes.engine: eight exact kernel evaluations plus the absorbing-zero and threshold-persistence lemmas
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Finite behaviour of the auxiliary recurrence only.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: These values do not state the concrete belowPulse values. In particular, the selected-late-cofactor hypothesis needed to relate the auxiliary floor to concrete rows fails on the seven measured classes.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: lateCofFloor, lateTotalFloor, and lateRun are periodic in the starting phase with period 2730; the recurrence equality extends to every multiple of that period. Since phase 20 never reaches zero, every phase 20+2730n also survives at every depth.
statement_nodes.engine: periodicity of the fixed pulse floor and modulo-three cofactor floor, induction on recurrence depth and period multiple
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Exact periodicity theorem for the auxiliary recurrence.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The infinite progression is an escape family for lateRun only. It is not a cofinal family of concrete greedy late skips and does not prove the #257 endpoint.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Among the 2730 residue phases D in [0,2730), exactly 87 satisfy lateRun D 12 != 0.
statement_nodes.engine: exhaustive decide +kernel computation over one full period
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A finite exact census of the auxiliary recurrence.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The count is only at depth 12 and does not claim that all 87 phases persist forever; named persistence results are separate. It is not a census of concrete #257 survivors.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A cofinal sequence of rows with LargestSkipLateAt yields skipped ranks tending to infinity and therefore 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set. Equivalently, cofinally many late rows suffice. Unconditionally, either from some row onward both cofactor-three solutions are always selected, or 1/2 belongs to the achievement set.
open_antecedents: To use the direct endpoint implication, one still needs a cofinal supply of LargestSkipLateAt rows; the finite certificates in this module do not provide it.
The unconditional final disjunction does not decide which branch holds.
statement_nodes.engine: late rank margin converts cofinal row growth into unbounded skipped-rank growth, followed by the established achievement-set endpoint; classical negation of eventual three-cofactor selection supplies cofinally many late rows
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Formal reduction and unconditional alternative internal to the #257 development.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This is the exact remaining fork, not a solution: the corpus proves neither eventual selection of both three-cofactors nor the cofinal late-skip branch independently. Erdős #257 remains open.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The arithmetic classification identifies meaningful late ranks, while the executable layer certifies concrete support failures and maximal false ranks.
All twenty-one statements are kernel-evaluated instances of rowChk soundness.
Each skipped odd three-cofactor instantiates the universal promotion from a late skip to a late largest skip.
Seven rows receive an independent structural proof in addition to the maximal-rank computation.
Some explicit cofactor skips both force a late row and witness failure of the stronger three-row hcof hypothesis.
The bundled finite disjunction is discharged by the twenty-one exact right-disjunct certificates.
The finite verdict records both the right-disjunct successes and failure of the left-route hypothesis.
It applies the general late-zone dichotomy only to the two arithmetically possible cofactor-three ranks.
The floor is available on the selection branch, but the global dichotomy does not establish that branch at all required rows.
lateRun is the recurrence induced by the smaller late-only floor and inherits its ceiling eleven.
The exact phase computations are propagated by the zero and threshold lemmas.
Periodicity transports the phase-20 persistence certificate to infinitely many starting phases.
The finite census measures one full period at depth twelve, while the progression theorem proves all-depth persistence for one periodic family.
The rowwise alternative is lifted to an eventual-selection versus cofinal-late endpoint dichotomy.
Twenty-one finite late rows do not supply the cofinal family required by the endpoint.
The periodic escape concerns only an auxiliary recurrence, not concrete late skips; confusing the two would falsely close the open endpoint.
